summary: postinstall downloads and executes an opaque binary from an anonymous file-sharing host
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall hook (scripts/install.js → src/download2.js) fetches a binary from the hardcoded URL https://sendit.sh/DAyiB/vZxBj.bat, writes it to ~/.celest/bin/chrome, chmods it 0o755, and launches it via puppeteer as the installer's 'Chromium' executable. sendit.sh is an anonymous file-sharing service with no relationship to any Chromium publisher; the URL is an opaque token with no version pinning, no hash or signature check, and the delivered bytes are unverifiable. Whoever controls that URL controls arbitrary code execution on every machine that installs the package. Additional context: the published package name 'testpackage83' and its description do not match the product identity used throughout the code and README ('celest-browser', ~/.celest paths, CELEST_SKIP_DOWNLOAD env var), consistent with a throwaway publication.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
